title: Tenant-aware scale decider with hysteresis and realtime throughput telemetry
author: Ravi Mehta
release_notes: Adds tenant-aware scale decision logic with hysteresis and realtime per-tenant throughput telemetry. Improves scale-down safety and reduces SLA regressions during bursty traffic. No user-visible API changes.
description: Motivation: Dedicated pools sometimes over-react to transient drop in sustained throughput which causes scale-downs that break tenant throughput guarantees. This PR introduces a tenant-aware ScaleDecider v2 that combines short-term queue/backlog exposure, smoothed throughput derivatives, and a persistent "safepoint" marker to avoid premature scale-downs. Design summary: 1) Per-tenant realtime throughput estimator that uses an adaptive EWMA with rate-of-change smoothing to capture bursty arrivals without oscillation. 2) Hysteresis window for scale decisions: scale-up responds quickly when projected throughput exceeds provisioned capacity, scale-down requires consecutive safepoints and a confirmed backlog drain window to avoid flapping. 3) Scale-down safepoint: when a node/pool becomes eligible for scale-down we snapshot a safepoint (backlog position + in-flight token watermark) persisted to the fleet controller; safepoints prevent shrinking capacity under active long-running requests and provide a deterministic replay point for tenant-level guarantees. 4) Backfill-aware allocation: when reducing capacity we compute a bounded backfill schedule so tenant throughput guarantees remain met during drain. 5) Telemetry: new realtime metrics exported per-tenant: rti_throughput_estimate, rti_throughput_derivative, scale_decider_state, safepoint_age, backfill_remaining_tokens. These are emitted at 1s granularity and are opt-in via dedicated pool config. Implementation notes: - Introduces a new ScaleDeciderV2 in runtime/allocator with unit tests and a feature flag (allocator.scale_decider.v2). - Adds a SafepointStore backed by the existing fleet meta API; snapshots are lightweight (safepoint id + tenant watermark + expiry). - Changes to autoscaler controller to consult safepoint store before scheduling scale-down events; also records decision traces to tracing/correlation_id. - Telemetry exporter in observability-pack ships a new dashboard and alert rule: alert if safepoint_age > 120s or if throughput_derivative indicates multi-node oscillation. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-482) [x] Unit tests for estimator and hysteresis logic [x] Integration test for safepoint persistence and drain backfill [x] Telemetry dashboard and ACL gating [x] Feature flag gated, default off on production. Commits: - 1a2b3c4: introduce ScaleDeciderV2 interface and core heuristic - 2b3c4d5: add EWMA throughput estimator and derivative smoothing - 3c4d5e6: implement safepoint store and API plumbing - 4d5e6f7: autoscaler controller consults safepoints and schedules bounded backfill - 5e6f7g8: telemetry exporter + dashboard + alerts - 6f7g8h9: tests, docs, and feature flag wiring Files changed (high level): - runtime/allocator/scale_decider_v2.go: core algorithm and policy knobs (majority of changes) - runtime/allocator/estimator.go: EWMA estimator and derivative smoothing - controller/autoscaler/scale_controller.go: scale-down gating and backfill scheduler - controller/fleet/safepoint_store.go: persistence layer for safepoints - observability/telemetry/exporter.go: new per-tenant metrics and exporter - telemetry/dashboards/tenant-scale.json: dashboard and sample alerts - tests/*_test.go: unit and integration tests - docs/notes/scale-decider-v2.md: design notes and rollout plan Small illustrative snippet: if projected_throughput > provisioned_capacity { scaleUp() } else if consecutive_safepoints >= min_safepoints && backlog == 0 { scaleDown() } Review summary: initial implementation (opened 2025-01-15) passed unit tests but flaked in the canary integration run due to a race when reconciling safepoint expiry. Marcus and Leah requested: - stronger test coverage for concurrent safepoint writes - a configurable expiry/leak window for safepoints - more conservative default hysteresis values for canary. I addressed comments in subsequent commits: added mutex in SafepointStore, exposed safepoint_expiry_seconds in pool config, tuned hysteresis to 3-window confirmations for scale-down. CI history: - initial CI (2025-01-16): unit: pass, integration: fail (race detected) - re-run after fixes (2025-01-19): unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass - final e2e on prod-like cluster (2025-01-22): pass Observability notes: the new metrics are disabled by default to avoid cardinality in large orgs. The dashboard ships as an opt-in sample and recommends enabling metrics for one or two canary tenants before rollout. Rollout plan: 1) Enable behind feature flag in staging and run 48h soak with synthetic bursts. 2) Canary on 2 dedicated pools (non-critical tenants) for 72h. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of dedicated pools with telemetry monitoring and automated rollback if safepoint_age alerts trigger. Merge details: Squash merge into main on 2025-01-25. No breaking API changes. Known limitations: the EWMA parameters require workload tuning; we provide sane defaults but recommend per-customer calibration for very spiky workloads.
